keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Roof area, rain, demand and losses determine useful storage
keyPoints.draft: Vhuhulwane ha roof, mvula, water demand na losses zwi laula uri hu nga vhulungwa maḓi mangana ane a shumisea.
keyPoints.literalBacktranslation: The size of the roof, rain, water demand and losses determine how much usable water can be stored.
keyPoints.uncertainty: Roof, water demand and losses remain English anchors; the mixed-language Tshivenda grammar and the term for useful storage need fluent review.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Size and maintain the first-flush diverter for the roof
keyPoints.draft: Size and maintain the first-flush diverter for the roof
keyPoints.literalBacktranslation: Size and maintain the first-flush diverter according to the roof.
keyPoints.uncertainty: Root targeted check retains exact source: uncertain technical imperative or matched-use wording.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Clear water can still contain germs or chemicals
keyPoints.draft: Clear water i nga kha ḓi vha na germs kana chemicals.
keyPoints.literalBacktranslation: Clear water can contain germs or chemicals.
keyPoints.uncertainty: The source's possibility remains explicit with i nga vha; clear, germs and chemicals stay English to avoid implying visibly clean water is safe.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Testing and treatment must match the intended use
keyPoints.draft: Testing and treatment must match the intended use
keyPoints.literalBacktranslation: Testing and treatment must correspond to the intended use.
keyPoints.uncertainty: Root targeted check retains exact source: uncertain technical imperative or matched-use wording.

question.sourceEnglish: What information is needed to choose a rainwater tank?
question.draft: Ndi mafhungo afhio ane a ṱoḓea u khetha rainwater tank?
question.literalBacktranslation: What information is needed to choose a rainwater tank?
question.uncertainty: Rainwater tank stays English as the technical object; question wording is a machine draft.

options.sourceEnglish: Only the province where the farm is located
options.draft: Province ine farm ya vha khayo fhedzi.
options.literalBacktranslation: Only the province where the farm is located.
options.uncertainty: Province and farm are retained as English anchors; only remains explicit.

options.sourceEnglish: Roof area, rainfall pattern, water demand and collection losses
options.draft: Vhuhulwane ha roof, pattern ya mvula, water demand na losses dza kuvhanganya maḓi.
options.literalBacktranslation: The size of the roof, rainfall pattern, water demand and water-collection losses.
options.uncertainty: The list preserves all four factors; technical anchors and mixed concord need fluent review.

options.sourceEnglish: Only the amount of rain in one storm
options.draft: Tshivhalo tsha mvula ya storm nthihi fhedzi.
options.literalBacktranslation: Only the amount of rain in one storm.
options.uncertainty: Storm remains an English term; one event and only are retained.

options.sourceEnglish: Only the price of the biggest available tank
options.draft: Mutengo wa tank khulwanesa ine ya wanala fhedzi.
options.literalBacktranslation: Only the price of the biggest tank that is available.
options.uncertainty: Tank remains English; the superlative and only are retained.

rationale.sourceEnglish: Tank planning must compare usable supply with demand through wet and dry periods. One fixed regional size cannot do that.
rationale.draft: U pulana tank hu tea u vhambedza supply ine ya nga shumiswa na demand kha wet na dry periods. Sayizi nthihi ya region yo tiwaho a i nga koni u ita zwenezwo.
rationale.literalBacktranslation: Tank planning must compare usable supply with demand during wet and dry periods. One fixed size for a region cannot do that.
rationale.uncertainty: The comparison and inability of one fixed regional size are retained. Wet and dry periods, supply, demand and region remain English anchors.

question.sourceEnglish: Why does a first-flush diverter matter even for irrigation-only tank water?
question.draft: Ndi ngani first-flush diverter i tshi thusa na musi maḓi a tank a tshi shumiswa kha irrigation fhedzi?
question.literalBacktranslation: Why does a first-flush diverter help even when tank water is used only for irrigation?
question.uncertainty: The irrigation-only limitation is preserved. First-flush diverter and irrigation remain English technical terms.

options.sourceEnglish: It doesn't matter for irrigation, only drinking water
options.draft: A i na mushumo kha irrigation; i thusa kha drinking water fhedzi.
options.literalBacktranslation: It has no importance for irrigation; it helps only for drinking water.
options.uncertainty: The distractor's only-drinking-water claim is retained; irrigation and drinking water remain English.

options.sourceEnglish: The first flush carries concentrated droppings, dust and pathogens that can contaminate edible crops
options.draft: First flush i hwala concentrated droppings, dust na pathogens dzine dza nga contaminate edible crops.
options.literalBacktranslation: The first flush carries concentrated droppings, dust and pathogens that can contaminate edible crops.
options.uncertainty: Concentrated, all three contaminant types, can-contaminate modality and edible crops are kept explicit in English.

options.sourceEnglish: It's more acidic and changes soil pH over time
options.draft: It's more acidic nahone i shandula soil pH nga tshifhinga.
options.literalBacktranslation: It is more acidic and changes soil pH over time.
options.uncertainty: The comparative more acidic and the soil-pH/time claim remain exact English to avoid changing the distractor.

options.sourceEnglish: It stops the tank overfilling in storms
options.draft: I thivhela tank uri i sa ḓadzehe nga maḓi manzhi nga storms.
options.literalBacktranslation: It prevents the tank from filling too much with water during storms.
options.uncertainty: Overfilling and the storm condition are retained; storm remains an English anchor.

rationale.sourceEnglish: Diverting early runoff can reduce contamination, but it does not guarantee that later water is safe. Assess quality for the intended use.
rationale.draft: U divert-a early runoff zwi nga fhungudza contamination, fhedzi a zwi khwaṱhisedzi uri maḓi a tevhelaho a tsireledzea. Ṱolani quality u ya nga intended use.
rationale.literalBacktranslation: Diverting early runoff can reduce contamination, but it does not guarantee that the later water is safe. Assess quality according to the intended use.
rationale.uncertainty: Can-reduce, no-guarantee, later water, and assessment for intended use are all preserved; runoff, contamination and quality remain English anchors.
